title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference: September 21, 2026
headline: Will Johnson's neck injury could cost him the season, and Max Melton is day-to-day with his own issue, so monitor the cornerback room before Sunday.
summary: LaFleur said the team is moving on from the loss to Seattle and will focus on a quick response at Wednesday's practice. He attributed the offensive struggles mainly to the inability to push the ball downfield against shell coverages, pointing to four early pass plays that never got deep, missed third-down conversions, and a second half he described as having no rhythm. He said the offense needs better drop steps, more completions, and some explosive plays, and that the run game has had moments, with the mid-zone working reasonably well and the duo game needing work. On Marvin Harrison Jr., he rejected the idea that his effort is lacking, saying his running style is just different and his teammates don't see it that way. He praised Trey McBride and Kendrick Bourne as underneath options while indicating the approach could change this week. On defense, he said he liked the effort, especially on the final goal-line stand. Injury updates were mixed: Max Melton is more day-to-day and will be evaluated Wednesday or Thursday, while Will Johnson has a neck injury that could potentially sideline him for the whole season. LaFleur said Starling is in a good spot physically and mentally after playing well, and he is not yet sure whether the Will Johnson injury will require surgery.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 3 Media Availability | Monday, September 21st | Press Conference
headline: Falcons QB decision (Penix vs. Strand/Rush) still pending before Thursday at Green Bay; Coach Stefanski will update after meeting players, and Kyle Pitts' snap share dipped.
summary: Stefanski opened by outlining a compressed short-week schedule ahead of Thursday night at Green Bay, with a walkthrough Monday, practice Tuesday, and travel Wednesday. He said there were no major injury updates yet, with more MRIs pending and an estimated practice report coming later. On the quarterback spot, he gave no update, saying he has a decent idea of direction but has not yet talked to the players, and he declined to comment on reports that Michael Penix Jr. is trending toward starting. He said he talks to Penix daily and is confident in the medical process, but gave no clearance. Tua Tagovailoa is 'getting better,' with what that means for this week still to be worked through. He called the offense's first two games not good enough, pointing to coaching, scheme, and execution, and said the turnover margin and complementary football were the core message to the team. He defended Kyle Pitts, saying the lowest snap share of his career shouldn't be overread, and said Pitts is a big part of the plan. He explained the fourth-down jet sweep to Drake London instead of Bijan Robinson as a call that didn't work, and said the process behind it was reasonable. He also said he chose to pull Cooper Rush because he believed it was best for the team in that moment, and he praised Jack Strand's development after Strand's first snap at quarterback.

title: Jesse Minter Reflects on Ravens' Week 2 Performance
headline: Trenton Simpson is playing like one of Baltimore's best defenders, Bateman and Andrews stepped up in Flowers' absence, and Zay Flowers, Ronnie Stanley, and Nnamdi Madubuike have a good shot to play in Rio.
summary: Minter opened by saying the Ravens will stay self-critical after the Week 2 loss to New Orleans, with the focus on all three phases and on closing out games. The team travels to Brazil to play Dallas, with a normal Wednesday practice, a Thursday evening flight, and a Friday recovery day before the Sunday game. He said the Rio field condition is in the league's hands and that both teams will play there. On the late-game decisions, he defended the third-and-one call and the kickoff choice, saying the team wanted to avoid giving up the ball in a tie game and wanted to keep the clock running. Defensively, he cited missed tackles on checkdowns, angles, and coverage breakdowns on third-and-long as the main problems. Operational penalties on offense, including false starts and motion penalties, are a major point of emphasis. He said Derrick Henry was himself in the game with no concerns. He praised Trenton Simpson as one of the team's best players right now and said Teddye Buchanan is coming back soon. He also said Rashod Bateman and Mark Andrews stepped up in the absence of a key receiver. On injuries, he said the team should have a good shot with many of the banged-up players this week, with a clearer picture expected Wednesday. He expressed confidence that Malaki Starks will bounce back, and said he wants to get a player who was used sparingly on defense more snaps.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: September 21st, 2026
headline: Monken calls the run game a fact that must improve, says Judkins' carries will rise with it, and treats Deshaun Watson's legs as a weapon.
summary: Monken said the rushing game (about 65 yards per game average) is a real problem that needs better scheming, coaching, play-calling, and blocking, and he acknowledged missed opportunities. He said the offense pivoted to quick throws and space passing in Week 2 because the defense was pressuring them on play-action and run plays. He praised Deshaun Watson's legs, citing third-down conversions, a design run, a scramble, and a naked-bootleg dump to Harold Fannin Jr., and said Watson has asked to be used as a runner. On defense, Monken credited cleaner execution, better play from Carson Schwesinger (defensive player of the game) and Mason Graham, and said the team won more interior one-on-one matchups than in Week 1. He defended the failed challenge, said he would go for it again on fourth-and-inches, and said he was more disappointed in the execution of that play. Monken said Tyson Campbell is dealing with several issues but he likes his chances to play, and he said the penalties and lost-yardage plays in the first half were the main problem. On the quarterback situation, Monken said Watson is still a young player who needs to improve his drops and reads and expects continued growth. He said Jerry Jeudy's targets will come and that more Judkins carries would mean fewer chances for the receivers.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “We Have to Handle Our Business” | Press Conference
headline: Malik Hooker is questionable for Rio after rehab, Cobie Durant (hamstring) and P.J. Locke (plantar fascia) are expected out a few weeks, and Jaishawn Barham and Markquese Bell earned praise.
summary: Schottenheimer gave a health update: Malik Hooker continues rehab and may be tough to have ready for the short week in Rio, though he isn't ruling him out. Cobie Durant has a hamstring strain and P.J. Locke has a plantar fascia tear, both could be out a few weeks, and no IR decision has been finalized. He said the field and grass concerns are not an issue because the league has people on site. On defense, he credited better communication, singled out Jaishawn Barham as a strong green-dot communicator who forced a fumble, and said Markquese Bell stepped in well when Locke went down. He said the pass rush was terrific but the unit must finish tackles and contain quarterbacks, and that run defense needs to improve before facing Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry in Baltimore. On offense, he said the run game has lagged because of limited possessions, too many backfield losses and a plan that leaned on throwing, and he praised Javonte Williams and the offensive line. He said George Pickens has been quiet but is making important catches and will be ready this week, and he praised Dak Prescott's accuracy and decision-making. He also highlighted Brevyn Spann-Ford's special teams play and Shemar James's extended action.

title: HC Sean Payton on Denver’s win in home opener: ‘I think our crowd was fantastic’
headline: Denver's backfield is unsettled: RJ Harvey sat Sunday and Jonah Coleman left early, and Payton would not name a lead back for Week 3.
summary: Payton said RJ Harvey was out Sunday and Jonah Coleman got nicked up and could not finish the Jacksonville game. He said none of the injuries were at a point where he could name a workhorse this Monday, and that the team has a lot to sort out this week about who its runners will be. On the offense, he said the identity has to show itself through urgency, since games where the first half fails will keep coming. He called the goal-to-go series from the one a poor possession overall, not a cadence problem. On defense, he said film review on tackling did not need to be long, because tackling is one of the three or four most important defensive jobs. He said the crowd was fantastic and that the communication breakdowns on formation changes, which forced Jacksonville timeouts, were a real issue. He called the quarterback-coaching change (Davis Webb) a matter of players and staff all getting up to speed, and described the fist bump as excitement after a win. On close games, he said the team's confidence from previous comebacks matters, but it is still working to avoid being in as many one-score games.

title: Campbell on perspective and improving
headline: Avonte Maddox needs surgery and is out for the season; Brian Branch won't play this week, and Ennis Rakestraw could get a look as Detroit reshuffles the secondary before the Jets.
summary: Campbell said Avonte Maddox will need surgery and is out for the season, calling him a good, solid player and saying the team has to move forward. He told the team to keep things in perspective: it is only Week 2, but they are already heading into Week 3, so they need urgency without panic. He called the defense's inconsistency and the offense's run game and explosive-play problems the main issues, and said third and fourth down conversion rates on both sides need cleaning up. He cited 18 penalties, 14 of them in his view avoidable, along with poor punt coverage and missed kickoff-return opportunities, and said all of it is correctable. Campbell said the defense is shuffling players and giving more snaps to earned contributors, and that Brad is working to bring in veteran and younger safeties. He said Brian Branch could return sooner than the player he called Kirby, but not this week, and that Kirby won't play until the knee is strong enough. He said Ennis and Ahmed, who have been inactive, are under consideration and that he is open to all options. He framed the Jets game as a chance to coach better, and he expressed confidence in defensive coordinator Shep and the staff.

headline: Mahomes looked sharper and Tyquan Thornton and Travis Kelce are being trusted, while Emmett Johnson is set to take more carries from Kenneth Walker III and Mansoor Delane was held back after being questionable.

He praised the team's performance across all three phases while stressing there is still room to improve, especially with a young roster that is learning through practice. He credited Patrick Mahomes with getting the ball out on time, making line-of-scrimmage checks accurately, and mixing up the snap count. He liked the offensive line's aggressiveness and the receivers and tight ends blocking and getting open against a man-heavy defense. Reid said Tyquan Thornton earned his big game after a strong camp and that he would expect similar opportunities. On Kenneth Walker III, Reid said Emmett Johnson will get more snaps over time, which will take some load off Walker, though Walker wants the ball every play. Mansoor Delane was not fully ready, and Reid kept him out of a full game to avoid stressing the injury. Reid said Travis Kelce worked hard in the offseason and is showing good explosiveness. He also said Rashee Rice's burst is coming back early in games after his knee procedure.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Sept 21 | Press Conference
headline: Hafley says Miami's secondary communication breakdowns and pre-snap penalties must be fixed, Chop Robinson is progressing through concussion protocol, and Malik Willis is showing accuracy but needs consistency.
summary: Hafley said it is too early to know whether Caleb Douglas's ankle injury will keep him out next Sunday. Chop Robinson has made progress in concussion protocol and is exactly where the staff expected, with a Wednesday update to come. Hafley praised Michael Taaffe's instincts and physicality after a team-high nine tackles, while noting he still has rookie cleanup to do. Austin Jackson has had good moments and tough ones against elite edge rushers, which Hafley framed as inconsistency rather than a major decline. On Malik Willis, Hafley cited accuracy, extending plays, deep shots, and rushing to keep drives alive, while pointing to timing and rhythm on drop-back passes as the main area to improve. Hafley said the secondary's busts were uncharacteristic and tied to communication and wrong calls, and that the team would correct them. He called the penalties, especially pre-snap ones in the critical area past the 40, unacceptable and in need of urgent attention. On the roster, Hafley confirmed the plan to sign Andre Jones from Buffalo's practice squad, which he said was motivated by both depth and special teams. He also said Jalen Tolbert's time will come, though he is currently a inactive veteran playing behind younger players.

title: Kellen Moore recaps win over Ravens 9/21/2026
headline: Kelvin Banks needs ankle surgery in the next few days with his return timeline unclear, and Martin Emerson is day-to-day with a shoulder injury.
summary: Kellen Moore called the Week 2 win a good result but said the team is nowhere near where it needs to be, and he praised the team's resiliency. On the injury front, he confirmed Kelvin Banks will have ankle surgery within a few days, with the timeline and any possible return this season to be determined afterward. He said Martin Emerson has a shoulder issue and is day-to-day. Asim Richards, who the team acquired last season, has improved in the offseason and will be asked to play a number of snaps this year, with David Edwards next to him helping stability. Moore praised Pete Werner's game, including 11 tackles and a sack, and said Tyler Shough is as tough as they come after taking hits on key downs. He said the run game had good moments, including cutbacks and Travis Etienne's runs, but it needs more consistency. The Juwan Johnson third-and-eight play changed the game and set up a goal-line chance, and Moore credited the offense for better communication against pressure. The Alvin Kamara and Travis Etienne backfield split was described as flow-of-game rather than planned, and CJ Donaldson was praised for pass protection and third-down work. The team plans to stay home for a few weeks ahead of the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3.

title: Aaron Glenn Press Conference (9/21) | Week 3
headline: Glenn says Garrett Wilson must get more involved in the offense, and Braelon Allen's touchdown run gives him a hopeful sign ahead of the Detroit game.
summary: Glenn opened by saying he'd have a better injury update Wednesday, and he was disappointed by the late collapse but encouraged by how the team dictated play for most of the game until about eight minutes into the fourth quarter. He defended the late-game decisions: avoiding a backed-up punt, going for it on fourth and one, and taking a field goal up two scores on the earlier drive, all made with his game management and analytics staff. He said the run game struggled against Green Bay's interior pressure, so the staff tried perimeter runs, and he pointed to Breece Hall's runs and Braelon Allen's touchdown run as positives. He acknowledged the offense needs to be more opportunistic and that Garrett Wilson must be more involved, calling it a point of emphasis. He said Geno Smith was distributing the ball well in the passing game. He also said special teams took a hit from injuries to starters, though he would not use injuries as an excuse. He praised the safeties for tackling well and keeping receivers in front of them. The team now turns its attention to Detroit.

title: WATCH: McCarthy Previews Week 3 against Bengals
headline: Pittman's Week 3 availability is unclear pending Wednesday's evaluation, while Max Iheanachor keeps earning more reps and the offensive line still needs continuity.
summary: McCarthy said the film showed a lot to like but several things to fix, and that the team needs to clean up its own house, starting with mental focus. He noted improvement in special teams and the return game and called the defense's point-total control and line-of-scrimmage play the top takeaways. Offensively he said the team didn't start fast, had too many three-and-outs on third down for two weeks in a row, and struggled with man-to-man pass protection. He admitted he was too hard on himself about practice volume during a hot Wednesday and Thursday, and said less volume and more creativity is a core principle he's working toward. On the offensive line he said the group needs continuity and more reps together, and that the staff will take a harder look at its concepts. He praised Max Iheanachor for improving every week, and said Troy Fautanu and Mason McCormick adapted naturally to moving from the right side to the left. He also said Michael Pittman's injury is different from his training camp issue and that he will be evaluated Wednesday, with no clear read on whether he plays Sunday. On the Bengals, he called Dexter Lawrence a major challenge and said the staff is pre-planning for both possible scenarios involving Joe Burrow, whose back flared up in practice and who will be evaluated Wednesday.

title: Shanahan Reacts to 49ers 35-13 Win Over Dolphins, Talks Purdy's Growth
headline: Purdy was sharp and McCaffrey reached 100 career TDs, but DeMarcus Robinson and Mike Evans left with ankle and hip injuries and the WR and DL depth is thin.
summary: Shanahan said Brock Purdy was very sharp and on point in the 35-13 win over Miami, hitting the right spots and making a perfect throw on the play that set up a goal-line score. He said the team felt normal after the travel because the days off and practice week got them back on track, and he was proud of the focus through a long road stretch. He praised George Kittle's touchdown catch after a double corner blitz opened the middle, and Christian McCaffrey's day, which included a 100th career touchdown. On injuries, Mike Evans's hip problem did not look serious, though he suspected a high ankle sprain and said it could change by tomorrow. Robinson and a defensive lineman did not return; Shanahan said both looked like high ankle sprains but he could not confirm yet. Jack Jones and Romello Height returned after foot and hand injuries. On the roster, Shanahan said the team has lost several receivers and about three defensive linemen, so it will likely add a player from the practice squad or a veteran, and a decision is expected by Wednesday. Asked about Brandon Aiyuk, he said no. He was not concerned about the run defense giving up big plays, and he expects to see more on tape.

Pineiro was rested and a kicker with an illness was a late question, but Shanahan said he was great and the team felt confident in him.
Shanahan said the team handled the travel and days off well and that staying focused at home was the biggest challenge.

title: Todd Bowles on Getting it Right: Capitalizing | Press Conference
headline: Bowles says Bucky Irving keeps the lead back role, Jalen McMillan's role will grow as he gets healthier, and Rueben Bain still needs more production.
summary: Bowles said the defense has to tackle better and execute more cleanly, pointing to missed tackles and a 15-yard facemask penalty on the Browns' scoring drive, and he said the team has to coach it better. He stood by linebacker Alex Anzalone, saying he is still confident in him and that several players need to clean up their play. He said the pass rush improved in Week 2 but still has to finish more plays. On Rueben Bain, he said the player reports his AC sprain is no longer a problem, but Bowles doesn't think he is fully healthy. He added that Bain is good enough to play and the production has to come. On offense, Bowles said the run game is working and the line is still building cohesion, but protection and stunt pickup need work. He attributed the holding penalties partly to Baker Mayfield's scrambling and said the team can't have those penalties. He said Jalen McMillan is close to full health and will get a bigger role once he is fully there. On the backfield, Bowles said Bucky Irving had the hot hand, so he got early work, and that Kenny Gainwell remains a key one-back who will also help on kick returns. He said the team will need Sean Tucker too, and that the long season will require all of them. He said the team's mood is angrily optimistic and that the Week 3 focus is Minnesota.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/21/26
headline: Jayden Daniels (elbow) has no return timeline until specialist visits this week; Marcus Mariota starts Sunday, and Brandon Coleman looks good to go.
summary: Dan Quinn said Jayden Daniels had imaging on his elbow, with specialist visits Tuesday and Wednesday, and he would not guess at a timeline until those results are in. He expects a clearer update Thursday or Friday, and he ruled out surgery being discussed after last year's injury, calling it part of the rehab plan. Quinn said Daniels is in good spirits, and he dismissed any talk of a brace or of adding a veteran backup for now. Marcus Mariota will start Sunday, and Quinn praised him as one of the team's greatest leaders. Nick Cross was held overnight in Dallas after an internal injury, was discharged, and is flying home; Quinn expects a timeline update Wednesday. Brandon Coleman's finger injury is trending well and he should be ready for practice, Javon Kinlaw will be limited all week by a shoulder injury pending imaging, and Samuel Cosmi has entered the concussion protocol. On defense, Quinn was frustrated by four touchdown passes allowed and poor communication in the secondary, and he wants more urgency in calls. The defense also has not forced turnovers yet, though Quinn saw good shots at the ball from Daron Payne and K'Lavon Chaisson, and he said the team is close to converting. Quinn said the team is disappointed at 0-2 but resolute, and it is excited for the home opener.
